functions.name: Open the browser experiment
functions.behaviour: Loads the isolated session snapshot, model structure and full-model rendering assets. The G1 layout initially shows the Grip/Twist workspace; G2 initially shows the working block with keyboard keys collapsed, and narrow layouts move the input selectors into the fixed keyboard strip.
functions.notes: HTTP handlers and the imported Renderer are dependencies defined outside S5. Reads and writes describe snapshot consumption and requested engine operations; browser-only focus, camera, form and visibility changes use writes=none. Source evidence does not certify runtime, Windows/DirectX or performance results.

functions.name: Browse the command index
functions.behaviour: Opens a searchable list of non-form command names; choosing a result closes the index and dispatches that command.
functions.notes: The corresponding result button is listed with each command below. Default F1 also works in a text field outside a modal when it still maps to index; modal and IME input retain ownership.

functions.name: Choose an orbit by structure
functions.behaviour: Searches mathematical orbit descriptions and previews a representative hosting-cell/affecting-cap arrangement. Use this orbit explicitly sends the selected orbit to the engine.
entry_points: window Choose an orbit by structure
button Choose an orbit by structure: <orbit description> (data-orbit-choice)
button Choose an orbit by structure: Use this orbit
functions.notes: Startup replaces the initial HTML orbitButton bank command with orbit before state enables dispatch; the pre-start placeholder is not an additional bank entry point.

functions.name: Choose and activate a keyboard bank
functions.behaviour: Searches banks by ID, purpose or name and displays their buffers, captured caps, requirements and associated macros. Selecting a row or using the search-field arrows changes the candidate, and explicit activation switches the engine bank and resets held input.
entry_points: button Grip / Twist workspace: Choose bank by ID
window Keyboard banks · choose by ID
button Keyboard banks · choose by ID: <bank ID and name> (data-bank-choice)
button Keyboard banks · choose by ID: Activate selected bank
functions.notes: A single search match becomes the candidate automatically. Default F2 may open this chooser from a non-modal text field; Enter activation is local to bankSearch.

functions.name: Return to the previous keyboard bank
functions.behaviour: Activates workspace.previous_bank and closes the bank chooser.
entry_points: button Keyboard banks · choose by ID: Previous bank

functions.name: Rename the current bank
functions.behaviour: Opens the current bank name for editing and saves the entered name without selecting another bank.
entry_points: button Keyboard banks · choose by ID: Rename current
button Rename current bank: Save name

functions.name: Switch to a bank family in the current orbit
functions.behaviour: Activates the bank formed from the current bank orbit and the explicitly chosen A, B, I, M or E suffix.

functions.name: Select or release an explicit Grip
functions.behaviour: A mapped physical key chooses its captured fixed cap using Hold or Latch behavior, while an onscreen Grip toggles a pointer selection. Multiple simultaneous grips disable the active grip, and selecting a grip leaves the camera and mechanical state unchanged.

functions.name: Choose Hold or Latch grip behavior
functions.behaviour: Changes how physical Grip presses are retained and resets current held, latched and pointer grips before further input.
entry_points: menu Keyboard: Grip behavior > Hold Grip
menu Keyboard: Grip behavior > Latch Grip
functions.notes: This selector is read directly from the DOM; its change handler sends no settings request.

functions.name: Enter a legal cap Twist
functions.behaviour: With one explicit active Grip, sends the chosen H/T axis and inverse flag together with the current state hash, destination and phase. Draft input remembers its previous recipe and switches to draft display; Live puzzle input requests a committed turn through the engine.

functions.name: Toggle inverse for onscreen Twists
functions.behaviour: Toggles the onscreen inverse flag and its button highlight; subsequent onscreen Twists read that flag.
functions.notes: This flag affects pointer Twists; physical Twists use the actual Shift key.

functions.name: Choose the input destination
functions.behaviour: Chooses Draft or Live puzzle for later turns, saves both destination and current phase through settings, and resets Grip input context.
entry_points: menu Operation desk: INPUT > Live puzzle

functions.name: Choose the keyboard input phase
functions.behaviour: Chooses Prepare, Macro or Cleanup for later draft turns, saves the phase and destination, and resets Grip input context.
functions.notes: Clicking a phase tile opens its recipe editor; it is a separate entry from this inputPhase selector.

functions.name: Capture or edit fixed cap mappings
functions.behaviour: Opens the active bank cap slots for explicit editing and applies a validated sequence of C1-C600 values. Empty trailing slots are trimmed, an interior gap is rejected, and applying the capture resets held input.
entry_points: button Grip / Twist workspace: Capture selected structure
button Capture fixed cap mappings: Apply explicit capture
functions.notes: The form contains one field per configured Grip code. Captures stay fixed until an explicit later capture; editing or staging a source does not apply it.

functions.name: Stage hosting or affecting cells for capture
functions.behaviour: Fills the capture form from the inspected piece hosting cells, inspected affecting caps, Buffer A caps or Buffer B caps. The candidate is applied only by Apply explicit capture.
entry_points: button Capture fixed cap mappings: Selected hosting cells
button Capture fixed cap mappings: Selected affecting caps
button Capture fixed cap mappings: Buffer A caps
button Capture fixed cap mappings: Buffer B caps

functions.name: Edit and save key bindings
functions.behaviour: Opens JSON configuration for commands, Twists and Grip codes, including per-bank overrides, and saves the edited mappings. A supplied global Grip list must contain twenty codes, and saving resets active input.
entry_points: button Editable key bindings: Save mappings
functions.notes: The browser validates JSON and the global Grip count here; further configuration validation is delegated to the settings handler. Ctrl+Enter/Meta+Enter and text, IME or modal ownership remain excluded by the router even when bindings are edited.

functions.name: Stage the editable default mappings
functions.behaviour: Replaces the key-binding text area with the default command, Twist and twenty Grip mappings plus an empty bank-override object. Saving remains a separate explicit action.
entry_points: button Editable key bindings: Show editable defaults

functions.name: Export the key-binding form
functions.behaviour: Downloads the current key-binding text area as magic600-keys.json, including edits that have not been saved.

functions.name: Switch the central workspace
functions.behaviour: Shows Work, Reference or Keys, or cycles through those three tabs. Work combines fixed buffer and destination sockets, occupants, block requirements and effect overlays; Reference shows actual cell groups, and Keys shows the active bank and structural examples.
functions.notes: The Work diagram distinguishes the selected macro body from a complete reviewed operation and shows frame changes and protection conflicts. Geometry and schematic effect graphics do not change the mechanical state.

functions.name: Show and filter Macro Base
functions.behaviour: Opens or closes Macro Base, focuses macro search, and filters existing entries by name/note/ID, active/all orbits and effect classification.
entry_points: button Macro Base: Close Macro Base (×)
menu Macro Base: Macro orbit scope > Active orbit
menu Macro Base: Macro orbit scope > All orbits
menu Macro Base: Macro classification > All effects
menu Macro Base: Macro classification > Star recipes
menu Macro Base: Macro classification > Personal
menu Macro Base: Macro classification > Orientation effects
functions.notes: F3 invokes macro-search, which opens and focuses the library; the Macro Base and close buttons invoke library-toggle. Layout rules initially hide the library for G1 and use a drawer on narrow screens.

functions.name: Inspect an existing macro effect
functions.behaviour: Selecting a macro requests its exact effect and applicability, displays its full support and fixed target information, and offers explicit insertion into a draft phase. Selection switches to Work when needed and returns the puzzle display to committed occupants.
functions.notes: A result row may initially say Unverified; selecting it requests the effect. This action does not insert the macro or choose a solving action.

functions.name: Input and save a concrete macro
functions.behaviour: Accepts a name, purpose note and explicit finite JSON recipe of word/star steps, then asks the engine to validate and save it.
entry_points: button Macro Base: + (Import an explicit finite recipe)
window Input and save a concrete macro
button Input and save a concrete macro: Validate and save

functions.name: Edit macro name and purpose
functions.behaviour: Opens the selected macro name and note and saves the entered metadata for that macro ID.
entry_points: button Macro name and purpose: Save notes

functions.name: Compare exact macro actions
functions.behaviour: Compares two explicitly selected library entries and displays full net equality, inverse status and orbit-local equality separately.
entry_points: button Compare exact macro actions: Compare full model

functions.name: Set an explicit reference word
functions.behaviour: Opens the current reference JSON word and saves the user-entered legal word as work context.
entry_points: button Explicit reference transform: Use this reference word
functions.notes: An empty word denotes the canonical reference. The browser does not search for a setup or choose a frame.

functions.name: Save a selected macro under a reference
functions.behaviour: Saves the reference word entered in the reference dialog and requests a transformed copy of the selected macro under that reference.
entry_points: button Explicit reference transform: Save selected macro under reference
functions.notes: The dialog describes chronological R inverse / Macro / R. No result is applied to the puzzle by this control.

functions.name: Edit an explicit phase recipe
functions.behaviour: Opens Prepare, Macro or Cleanup as JSON chronological recipe steps and saves the edited phase to the draft after retaining a window-local undo copy.
entry_points: button Grip / Twist workspace: Inspect entered word
window Edit prepare · explicit chronological recipe
window Edit macro · explicit chronological recipe
window Edit cleanup · explicit chronological recipe
button Phase recipe editor: Apply draft edit
functions.notes: F4 edits the phase currently chosen in inputPhase; clicking a phase tile opens that specific editor without changing the keyboard phase selector.

functions.name: Append a macro to Prepare
functions.behaviour: Appends the explicitly selected or dragged macro to Prepare and retains a local undo copy of the prior draft.
functions.notes: A drop assigns the dragged macro ID before insertion; clicking the phase tile instead edits its recipe.

functions.name: Use a macro as the Macro phase
functions.behaviour: Replaces the Macro phase with the explicitly selected or dragged macro and retains a local undo copy of the prior draft.
entry_points: button Macro effect actions: Use as Macro

functions.name: Append a macro to Cleanup
functions.behaviour: Appends the explicitly selected or dragged macro to Cleanup and retains a local undo copy of the prior draft.

functions.name: Undo a draft edit in this window
functions.behaviour: Restores all three draft phases from the most recent window-local undo copy, sending Prepare, Macro and Cleanup in order. It reports an error when no saved draft edit remains.
functions.engine_call: POST /api/experiment/command action=draft phase=prepare; POST /api/experiment/command action=draft phase=macro; POST /api/experiment/command action=draft phase=cleanup
functions.notes: The browser retains at most thirty draft copies. This is distinct from undo of committed journal operations.

functions.name: Set Cleanup to the inverse of Prepare
functions.behaviour: Remembers the current draft and asks the engine to replace Cleanup with the inverse of Prepare.

functions.name: Review the complete operation
functions.behaviour: Requests a complete-operation review, clears the selected macro-body overlay and shows Work. The UI displays review status, goal and prefix status, full effect information and protection-conflict controls.

functions.name: Preview a reviewed operation
functions.behaviour: Sends the current review ID for preview; the Preview button is enabled only when the review status is Ready, and an absent review is rejected.
functions.notes: This control requests engine preview authorization; it is distinct from viewing predicted occupants with Draft result.

functions.name: Commit the previewed operation
functions.behaviour: Requests commit, returns the display to committed state and refreshes the snapshot. The Commit preview button is enabled only when the snapshot says the operation is executable.
functions.notes: The browser delegates legality, revision/hash checks and the Session transaction to the engine commit handler; this inventory records that call, not an independent proof of those checks.

functions.name: Cancel a preview
functions.behaviour: Requests cancellation of the engine preview without committing the proposed operation.

functions.name: Cancel active analysis
functions.behaviour: Sends a stop-job request and displays that cancellation was requested with committed state preserved. The dedicated Cancel analysis button is visible while an operation is busy.
functions.notes: The UI requests cancellation without waiting for a separate acknowledgement here; asynchronous command completion is handled by api job polling.

functions.name: View committed occupants
functions.behaviour: Selects the committed-state display, redraws the diagrams and reinstalls the committed renderer frame from the last render snapshot.

functions.name: View the proposed draft result
functions.behaviour: Requires a nonempty draft, requests a complete review and shows predicted occupants in the diagrams and puzzle frame. Puzzle picking is disabled in the proposed view.
functions.notes: The workspace follows the supplied source-to-destination cycles; when the cycle catalogue is truncated it marks uncaptured occupants unknown rather than assuming they stay put.

functions.name: Inspect exact operation effects
functions.behaviour: Opens the selected macro effect or current review effect as support, directed cycles, fixed-position orientation changes and slot-pair data, together with the reference. The dialog labels a truncated slot-pair display when only the first 160 pairs are included.
entry_points: button Macro effect actions: Exact effects
functions.notes: No additional engine request is issued by the dialog; it displays the effect already returned by macro inspection or review.

functions.name: Inspect a piece identity
functions.behaviour: Activating an identity token or a picked sticker in a current committed puzzle frame requests inspection of that identity. A Shift-modified puzzle pick also opens the Current/destination dialog after inspection.
entry_points: button Work canvas: Inspect identity I<piece> (data-identity)
button Puzzle viewport: picked sticker (Renderer callback)
functions.notes: Sticker picking resolves the identity from the renderer labels and slot-to-piece table and rejects stale, busy or proposed frames. Inspection does not itself change Current, destination or Grip capture.

functions.name: Inspect a fixed position or position conflict
functions.behaviour: Activating a fixed position socket or a protection-conflict button requests inspection of that position and its occupant, clearing the browser-only selected cell.
entry_points: button Work canvas: Inspect fixed P<position> (data-position)
button Macro effect findings: Conflict at P<position> inspect protected position (data-conflict-position)

functions.name: Select a canonical cell for inspection
functions.behaviour: Selects a hosting cell, Home cell, affecting cap or projected/group cell and updates the selection text. It leaves the camera and Grip mapping unchanged until an explicit locate or capture action.
entry_points: button Local structure: current hosting C<cell> / S<slot> (data-cell)
button Local structure: Home C<cell> / Sticker<label> (data-cell)
button Local structure: affecting cap C<cell> (data-cell)
button Global or Reference diagram: projected C<cell> (data-cell)
button Global or Reference diagram: group A/B C<cell> (data-cell)
button Choose an orbit by structure: representative C<cell> (data-cell)
functions.notes: The cell selection is browser-only and does not call the engine. Controls in an orbit preview also use the shared data-cell handler.

functions.name: Choose a structural example as Current
functions.behaviour: Sends focus for the explicit 1-cell, 2-cell or 20-cell identity, or for the five-cell identity supplied by the structure response. If the five-cell example is not yet available, it reports that the fixture is loading.
functions.notes: These examples send focus with identity only; they do not import practice state or insert a macro.

functions.name: Choose Current and a fixed destination
functions.behaviour: Opens typed piece-identity and fixed-position fields, validates their ID kinds and saves Current with its explicit destination. Choosing Current does not select or insert a macro.
entry_points: button Experimental Workbench: Choose a piece / <Current identity at position> (currentButton)
button Current piece and destination: Make Current
functions.notes: When an inspected piece exists, the destination form defaults to its Home position (the piece ID), not to the previous workspace target. A Shift puzzle pick reaches this dialog through S5-41.

functions.name: Manage the locked Next bookmark
functions.behaviour: Opens the current identity bookmark and its position, with explicit locate, replacement, clear and activation controls. The dialog explains that the bookmark does not protect mechanical state.
entry_points: button Experimental Workbench: Manage locked Next (…)

functions.name: Pin or explicitly replace Next
functions.behaviour: Pins the inspected identity as Next; when Next already exists, it first opens an explicit replacement confirmation. Confirming sends the inspected identity with replace=true.
entry_points: button Locked Next · identity bookmark: Replace with inspected identity
button Replace locked Next?: Replace Next explicitly
functions.notes: Next follows an identity; it is separate from both position/orbit protection and Current activation.

functions.name: Clear the Next bookmark
functions.behaviour: Explicitly clears the locked Next bookmark through the engine.
entry_points: button Locked Next · identity bookmark: Clear bookmark

functions.name: Activate the bookmarked Next
functions.behaviour: Remembers the current draft, requests explicit Next activation and clears the selected effect overlay. The main Activate button is disabled when no Next exists.
entry_points: button Locked Next · identity bookmark: Activate explicitly

functions.name: Locate Next without activating it
functions.behaviour: Inspects the bookmarked identity and focuses the puzzle camera on its first current hosting cell. It reports that Current and destination remain unchanged and rejects an absent bookmark.
entry_points: button Experimental Workbench: <Next identity at position> / Not assigned (nextButton)
button Locked Next · identity bookmark: Locate

functions.name: Add the inspected identity to the working block
functions.behaviour: Requests a block requirement for the explicitly inspected identity.
entry_points: button Experimental Workbench: Add to block

functions.name: Protect the inspected fixed position
functions.behaviour: Requests an exact-label position lock for the inspected piece current position. The UI describes preservation at the complete-operation boundary.
functions.notes: The requested lock belongs to the fixed position, rather than to the identity that may later occupy it.

functions.name: Assign explicit A and B buffer positions
functions.behaviour: Opens the current A/B roles as typed fixed positions and saves the entered pair. Role assignment changes work context without relocating a macro or moving an occupant.
entry_points: button Experimental Workbench: A / B roles
window Explicit A / B buffer positions
button Explicit A / B buffer positions: Assign roles

functions.name: Inspect and apply protection policy
functions.behaviour: Displays whole-orbit checkboxes, exact position locks and the current net/position/prefix conflicts. Apply policy sends the chosen orbit locks and then the requested strict intermediate-primitive preservation flag.
entry_points: button Macro effect findings: Conflict in <orbit structure> / <affected pieces>
button Orbit and block protection: Apply policy
functions.notes: The dialog names Require preservation at every intermediate primitive. Whole-orbit and position locks are distinct, and the displayed policy applies to hidden pieces as well as visible pieces.

functions.name: Clear all protected positions explicitly
functions.behaviour: Enumerates the current position locks and sends block-protect with enabled=false for each one, then closes the dialog.
entry_points: button Orbit and block protection: Clear position locks explicitly
button Command index: protection clear positions

functions.name: Compose and apply a piece display filter
functions.behaviour: Opens the current filter expression and a Replace, Intersect, Union or Subtract operation, then explicitly applies them through the engine. The filter changes work display/picking membership while mechanical analysis and protection retain full scope.
entry_points: menu Piece Filter workbench: filter operation > Replace
menu Piece Filter workbench: filter operation > Intersect
menu Piece Filter workbench: filter operation > Union
menu Piece Filter workbench: filter operation > Subtract

functions.name: Preview filter counts
functions.behaviour: Sends the entered filter expression and operation with preview=true and displays the returned counts/data without applying the filter.
entry_points: button Piece Filter workbench: Preview counts

functions.name: Stage a filter preset expression
functions.behaviour: Replaces the filter text field with active, active & unsolved, everything or orientation_wrong. A separate Preview or Apply control evaluates or applies the expression.
entry_points: button Piece Filter workbench: Active orbit
button Piece Filter workbench: Unsolved active
button Piece Filter workbench: All pieces
button Piece Filter workbench: Orientation only

functions.name: Load a saved filter into the form
functions.behaviour: Choosing a named saved filter copies its stored expression into the filter field without applying it.
entry_points: menu Piece Filter workbench: Saved filters > <saved name>

functions.name: Save the current active filter
functions.behaviour: Sends the entered name to save the current filter and displays a Saved current filter message.
entry_points: button Piece Filter workbench: Save current
functions.notes: This request sends the name only; an edited but unapplied filterExpr is not sent by Save current.

functions.name: Browse reusable manual work sheets
functions.behaviour: Opens the saved work-sheet selector, name field and summary of the current three draft phases. Saving current work and reusing selected fixed steps remain explicit controls.

functions.name: Save the current work sheet
functions.behaviour: Sends a name to save the current fixed manual steps and explicit reference as a reusable work sheet, then closes the dialog.
entry_points: button Reusable manual work sheets: Save current

functions.name: Reuse a fixed work sheet
functions.behaviour: Remembers the current draft and requests the selected named work sheet, then closes the dialog. The dialog states that reuse retains the solver ownership of Current/Next and does not restore old safety results or choose another macro.
entry_points: button Reusable manual work sheets: Reuse fixed steps

functions.name: Open the linked Local view
functions.behaviour: Shows the inspected/current piece exact physical-slot-to-sticker-label correspondence, current and Home cells, orientation/solved status and affecting caps. Opening Local sets the linked panel to its local structure view.
functions.notes: Cell controls in this view are inventoried under S5-43; the view itself does not capture grips or change a reference.

functions.name: Open the linked Global view
functions.behaviour: Shows actual projected tetrahedral cells for the inspected piece hosting group and the target hosting group, with group membership, shared cells and shared-face counts. It requires the model W/X/Y/Z geometry and displays a waiting message rather than substituting geometry.
functions.notes: The projection, tetrahedral edges and adjacency are inspection graphics, not legal turns. No browser control in this shard supplies the optional globalDiagram angle.

functions.name: Open the actual puzzle panel
functions.behaviour: Opens the linked puzzle viewport and asks the renderer to fit it. The frame title and message distinguish committed state from the read-only proposed draft result, and renderer feedback reports mode and visible slot count or an error.
functions.notes: Renderer implementation and its own camera gestures are outside these six files; only the imported callbacks and method calls defined here are inventoried.

functions.name: Reset the puzzle camera
functions.behaviour: Focuses renderer cell index zero and fits the view, displaying that puzzle and work context are unchanged.
entry_points: button Actual puzzle viewport: Reset view

functions.name: Locate Current in the puzzle camera
functions.behaviour: Focuses the first current hosting cell of Current; an absent Current produces a Choose Current first error.
entry_points: button Actual puzzle viewport: Locate Current

functions.name: Locate the inspected selection or cell
functions.behaviour: Opens the puzzle view and focuses the explicitly selected cell, or the inspected piece first current hosting cell when no cell is selected.

functions.name: Choose the puzzle render mode
functions.behaviour: Selects Adaptive, Full mesh or Point glyphs, changes the renderer mode and requests a rebuild. Picking is disabled until the updated frame becomes coherent.
entry_points: menu Actual puzzle viewport: Puzzle render mode > Adaptive
menu Actual puzzle viewport: Puzzle render mode > Full mesh
menu Actual puzzle viewport: Puzzle render mode > Point glyphs
functions.notes: The DOM values are auto, mesh and points. This change handler does not save a preference or issue an engine command.

functions.name: Close linked panels or dismiss auxiliary views
functions.behaviour: Close linked views hides the Local/Global/Puzzle deck and restores prior focus when possible. Escape outside a dialog also hides Macro Base and returns focus to the central canvas.
entry_points: button Linked views: Close linked views (×)

functions.name: Close a browser dialog
functions.behaviour: The shared Close dialog button submits its dialog form; after closure, the router resets held keys and focus returns to the opener when it still exists, otherwise to the canvas.
functions.notes: All named modal windows share this close control. The source uses native HTML dialog/form behavior; it does not install a separate application Escape-to-close binding for a modal.

functions.name: Copy the inspected piece ID
functions.behaviour: Copies the inspected/current identity in I-prefixed form to the clipboard and reports success or an error.
functions.notes: Clipboard output is not a persisted engine-state, workspace or file write.

functions.name: Open the isolated session controls
functions.behaviour: Displays experiment source, build and model identity and provides practice, journal, checkpoint, reset, export and engine-stop controls. The panel identifies the isolated browser experiment and states its source/evidence limitations.

functions.name: Load explicit E1 practice
functions.behaviour: Requests the named E1 fixture, clears selected macro/effect and draft-result display, and closes the dialog. The UI identifies E1 as synthetic practice loaded through an explicit legal recipe.
entry_points: button Isolated experiment session: Load explicit E1 practice
functions.notes: The source message recommends a manual node-0 inverse choice in Macro Base; this control does not itself select or execute that inverse.

functions.name: Undo a committed operation
functions.behaviour: Requests Session undo and closes the session dialog.
entry_points: button Isolated experiment session: Undo committed

functions.name: Redo a committed operation
functions.behaviour: Requests Session redo and closes the session dialog.
entry_points: button Isolated experiment session: Redo committed

functions.name: Save a checkpoint
functions.behaviour: Requests a checkpoint using the entered name, or leaves the name unspecified for engine naming, then closes the dialog.
entry_points: button Isolated experiment session: Save checkpoint

functions.name: Restore a checkpoint
functions.behaviour: Requests restore of the selected checkpoint name, closes the dialog and clears the selected effect overlay.
entry_points: button Isolated experiment session: Restore checkpoint

functions.name: Reset the puzzle with a recovery point
functions.behaviour: Requests reset, closes the dialog and returns to committed-state display. The success message states that the previous solve remains in a recovery checkpoint.
entry_points: button Isolated experiment session: Reset puzzle with recovery point
functions.notes: Transactional reset and recovery retention are implemented by the engine dependency, not proven by this browser source.

functions.name: Export work definitions
functions.behaviour: Downloads the complete current workspace JSON as magic600-experimental-work.json.
entry_points: button Isolated experiment session: Export work definitions
functions.notes: This is a workspace-definition download; the browser does not export the Session database or journal through this control.

functions.name: Stop the owned isolated experiment engine
functions.behaviour: When idle, reads the engine launch ID from health and sends authenticated shutdown with that ID. On success it closes the dialog, detaches keyboard input, stops renderer activity and reports that the engine has stopped and may be relaunched to resume.
entry_points: button Isolated experiment session: Stop experiment
functions.notes: Busy work must finish or have its analysis cancelled before shutdown. The browser uses its supplied token and the health reply launch_id; the actual process owner is outside this shard.

functions.name: Show or hide keyboard keys
functions.behaviour: Toggles visibility of the onscreen Grip/Twist keys and updates Keyboard aria-expanded. The bank and Grip metadata remain in the keyboard strip.
functions.notes: G2 starts with keyboard keys hidden; G1 starts with them shown.

internal_only.name: raw: authenticated JSON HTTP transport
internal_only.reason: Supplies the token header, serializes POST bodies and turns HTTP/error replies into exceptions; user actions and their outgoing route dependencies are listed in function rows. This shard defines no server HTTP handlers.

internal_only.name: api: command submission and route GET /api/job/<job_id> polling
internal_only.reason: Submits to the other-shard route POST /api/experiment/command and polls an asynchronous job every 45 ms until completion. The job-polling route is infrastructure behind user commands, not a separate browser action.

internal_only.name: send/adopt/refresh: snapshot adoption and route GET /api/experiment/snapshot refresh
internal_only.reason: Automatically installs returned workspace/snapshot state, resets input on a bank switch and refreshes changed state when a render payload is absent. Initial snapshot loading is covered by S5-1.

internal_only.name: run: operation busy state, non-queueing feedback and duration
internal_only.reason: Serializes work at the browser level, reports busy input as not queued and updates connection/duration indicators. Cancel analysis is the user entry point listed separately.

internal_only.name: decode/installRender: coherent committed or predicted frames
internal_only.reason: Decodes labels/styles, selects render versus predicted data and enables picking only for a matching committed hash. These are frame-installation callbacks behind the display functions.

internal_only.name: initializeRenderer: static geometry and Renderer setup
internal_only.reason: Loads mesh metadata and six binary arrays, constructs the imported Renderer and sets background/pixel scale. The startup row lists the outgoing asset dependencies; Renderer gestures defined in its own module are outside S5.

internal_only.name: renderer window visibility and unload lifecycle
internal_only.reason: Automatically suspends/resumes animation on visibility changes and terminates the worker/router on unloading. There is no additional user command or persisted model change.

internal_only.name: bindings/defaultCommands/defaultGripKeys/defaultTwists
internal_only.reason: Merges defaults, saved global overrides and saved current-bank overrides. Every defined default command chord and Grip/Twist code is assigned to a function row; the map construction is internal.

internal_only.name: DOM lookup, escaping, key labels and snapshot selectors
internal_only.reason: Presentation and selection helpers without their own command, button, window or key binding.

internal_only.name: orbitProfile/orbitName/orbitDefinition/macroName
internal_only.reason: Formats retained mathematical descriptions and macro labels for visible controls. It does not choose an orbit or transform the model.

internal_only.name: draw and panel/list composers
internal_only.reason: Renders the snapshot into the already inventoried panels, counts, macro rows, bank/orbit candidates and action buttons. Re-rendering is not a distinct user entry point.

internal_only.name: openDialog/closeDialog/showViews helpers
internal_only.reason: Shared modal/panel creation, input reset and focus bookkeeping. The windows and user close/open controls are listed in function rows.

internal_only.name: requireSelection guard
internal_only.reason: Rejects identity-requiring commands when no inspected/current piece exists; no independent user action.

internal_only.name: rememberDraft window-local undo copies
internal_only.reason: Deep-copies the three draft phases and retains at most thirty snapshots for the draft-undo entry point. It does not save checkpoints or undo committed journal state.

internal_only.name: download Blob/link helper
internal_only.reason: Produces local JSON downloads and revokes the object URL after use; key export and workspace export are the user entries.

internal_only.name: fitCompactInput and responsive CSS layout
internal_only.reason: Automatically relocates input controls and lays out drawers, linked views and the fixed keyboard strip as the window size changes. No additional button, menu or command is defined by CSS.

internal_only.name: focused diagram scrolling and canvas overflow indication
internal_only.reason: Native scrollable areas and focus/resize callbacks reveal offscreen diagram objects; there is no custom pan command or key binding in this shard.

internal_only.name: message/report and window frontend error feedback
internal_only.reason: Displays operation and frontend errors/status; these notifications are outputs of other functions, not separate user actions.

internal_only.name: KeyboardRouter attach/dispose/reset/input-context tracking
internal_only.reason: Owns event listeners and clears held/latched/pointer input on context, focus, IME, cancellation or visibility changes. Old held keys remain blocked until released.

internal_only.name: KeyboardRouter text/chord/event ownership and suppressed execution keys
internal_only.reason: Ctrl+Enter and Meta+Enter are explicitly suppressed as global execution shortcuts; modal, capture, text and IME contexts keep keyboard ownership. Ctrl/Control chord spelling is accepted; unmodified F1/F2 are exceptions for non-modal text navigation when bound to index/bank. These guarded keys do not define additional execution functions.

internal_only.name: KeyboardRouter active-grip, unavailable, repeat and key-release guards
internal_only.reason: Validates one active C1-C600 grip and a supported H/T axis, rejects busy/pending/repeated turns and releases blocked key codes. The Grip and Twist actions are inventoried under S5-8 and S5-10.

internal_only.name: parseId/specification/checkedNumber: typed ID validation
internal_only.reason: Shared validation behind typed Current/destination, buffer and cap fields; prefixes are case-sensitive and a bare decimal is interpreted only in its supplied kind. No independent parse/import control exists here.

internal_only.name: typed ID formatters, including orbit/frame presentation
internal_only.reason: Adds I/P/C/S/Sticker/O prefixes and scoped orbit/node text, with Fixed as a display sentinel. These are label helpers, not mechanical relabelling or user commands.

internal_only.name: cellFromSlot/labCellIndex: presentation index conversions
internal_only.reason: Maps a sticker slot to a 1-based canonical cell and converts a canonical cell to a 0-based Renderer index. Called behind Local correspondence and explicit locate controls.

internal_only.name: graphics primitives/control/wrap/occupantMap/socket helpers
internal_only.reason: Builds escaped SVG, fixed-position sockets and identity/cell controls from supplied snapshot data. Controls instantiated by the reachable diagrams are assigned to the identity, position or cell inspection rows.

internal_only.name: blockDiagram exported alternative
internal_only.reason: No caller/import in the six shard files renders this separate block-only diagram; the reachable Work tab uses workspaceDiagram. Its template position/identity controls have no independent browser entry point.

internal_only.name: operationDiagram exported alternative
internal_only.reason: No caller/import in the six shard files renders this separate operation diagram; reachable effect overlays use workspaceDiagram and exact details use a dialog. Its template position/identity controls are not additional user entries.

internal_only.name: globalDiagram optional angle parameter
internal_only.reason: All three browser call sites omit angle and use its zero default. There is no user rotation control for this SVG projection in the shard.
